## New Data: clean up and join 

### Step 1: Clean Up Dwell Data

The Hawaii data comes to us raw in text files, similar to Oahu. Here we will just generate the same summary tables as we did for Oahu. We will have to read in each excel file here and do some cleaning. 

This report should tell us:

- total number of TMKS assessed each year for Oahu
- how many TMKS are single owner versus multiple owner per year of data
- how many TMKS have more than one card (i.e. more than one building assessed on the parcel) per year
- Summary of bedrooms and bathrooms per year?


This might get long - the Hawaii dwell data is quite messy. A few notes from the data sent by the county: 

2010 - 2012 data did not come with extract formula sheets with them

I realized that specification docs were included for all years after 2012. I looked at them all side by side and there appear to be two distinct versions. The first (A) applies only to 2013, and 2019 - 2023. The second one (B) applies to 2014 - 2018.

They are actually identical until the year built column, which makes sense because when I was applying the ones above to different groups of years, the column that clued me into if it was working or not was year built. 

In A, yrbuilt is 434 to 437
In B, yrblt is 425 to 429

For Hawaii, Iʻm going to try a slightly different approach where I filter before worrying about the column parsing. Just to make things lighter 


```{r}

library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(janitor)

# read in HI iws permits

iws_permit_data <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "osds/shared-data/2009_Present_IWSList_Permits.csv"))


# filter out just the permits in Hawaii, and create permit ID tracker

iws_hi_permits <- iws_permit_data %>% 
  mutate(tmk_char = as.character(TMK)) %>% 
  filter(str_starts(tmk_char,"3")) %>% 
  rename(full_taxid = tmk_char) %>%  
  rowid_to_column("permit_id") # 7347

tmks_permits <- iws_hi_permits$full_taxid

# function to go get and read in each text file, parse, and filter
read_and_filter_hi_dwell <- function(year, driver_dir, col_specs, tmks_permits) {
  file_path <- file.path(driver_dir,
                         "4_OSDS_N_Runoff/large-input-data/Dwelling_Data_Raw/Hawaii_DwellRaw_12182025",
                         as.character(year),
                         "DWELDAT.TXT")
  
  read_fwf(file_path,
           col_positions = col_specs,
           na = c("", "NA"),
           col_types = cols(.default = col_character())) %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), ~trimws(.))) %>%
    # Rename first two columns
    rename(jursi_id = 1, tmk = 2) %>%
    # Create tmk_13 and tmk_9
    mutate(
      tmk_13 = paste0(jursi_id, tmk),
      tmk_9  = substr(tmk_13, 1, nchar(tmk_13) - 4)
    ) %>%
    # Filter by the TMKs we care about
    filter(tmk_9 %in% tmks_permits)
}

# next, apply function for years that correspond to each Spec 

yearsA <- c(2019:2023)

yearsA_list <- map(yearsA, ~read_and_filter_hi_dwell(.x, driver_dir, colspec_A, tmks_permits))
yearsA_df <- do.call(rbind, yearsA_list)


yearsB <- c(2013:2018)

yearsB_list <- map(yearsB, ~read_and_filter_hi_dwell(.x, driver_dir, colspec_B, tmks_permits))
yearsB_df <- do.call(rbind, yearsB_list)


# experiment: try b on A years? this seems to work better

yearsAbyB_list <- map(yearsA, ~read_and_filter_hi_dwell(.x, driver_dir, colspec_B, tmks_permits))
yearsAbyB_df <- do.call(rbind, yearsAbyB_list) 

# last bit: try both col spec versions on 2010 - 2012. 
yearsC <- (2010:2012)
yearsCbyA_list <- map(yearsC, ~read_and_filter_hi_dwell(.x, driver_dir, colspec_A, tmks_permits))
yearsCbyA_df <- do.call(rbind, yearsCbyA_list)

yearsCbyB_list <- map(yearsC, ~read_and_filter_hi_dwell(.x, driver_dir, colspec_B, tmks_permits))
yearsCbyB_df <- do.call(rbind, yearsCbyB_list)

# weirdly, while A was close in column it was split, while B was not split just behind. But I think A i feel safer about

dwell_2010_2012 <- yearsCbyA_df %>% 
  mutate(year_built_fixed = paste0(YRBLT,substr(EFFYR,1,1))) %>% #paste together year and the first character of eff year
  mutate(effective_year_fixed = paste0(substr(EFFYR,2,nchar(EFFYR)), substr(COND,1,1))) %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  select(jursi_id,
         tmk,
         tmk_9,
         taxyr,
         card,
         fixbath,
         fixhalf,
         rmtot,
         rmbed,
         yrblt = year_built_fixed,
         effyr = effective_year_fixed)
  


# select colums needed and bind all together

dwell_2013_2023 <- rbind(yearsAbyB_df, yearsB_df) %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  select(jursi_id,
         tmk,
         tmk_9,
         taxyr,
         card,
         fixbath,
         fixhalf,
         rmtot,
         rmbed,
         yrblt,
         effyr)

# bind all together!


allyears_hi_dwell <- rbind(dwell_2010_2012, dwell_2013_2023) %>% 
  rename(full_taxid = tmk_9)



# save

write_csv(allyears_hi_dwell, 
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/dwellings/hi_dwell_clean_2010_2023_permitTMKonly.csv"))


```

Ok so it looks like col Spec B has worked really well for all years. Who knew! Iʻm going to quickly check for any mistakes below, then we can move on.

```{r}

# create new column with length of yearbuilt, and print unique instances

unique(allyears_dwell$yearblt_length) # 4 and NA

# look at the NAS

allyears_dwell_yrblt_Na <- allyears_dwell %>% filter(is.na(yearblt_length))

# which years does this apply to?

unique(allyears_dwell_yrblt_Na$TAXYR) # since 2019
```

Hmm ok so I think I actually did not solve the parsing problem, and 2019 - 2023 did not parse correctly. Above, I went back and used col spec A on 2019 - 2023, and B for the rest. 

### Step 2: Bring in IWS data

Here we join dwell data to the permit information for the ones that correspond to dwellings, and save the list of non-dwell TMKS.

```{r}

# read in clean dwelling data

allyears_hi_dwell <- read_csv(file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/dwellings/hi_dwell_clean_2010_2023_permitTMKonly.csv")) %>% 
  mutate(full_taxid = as.character(full_taxid))

# read in HI iws permits

iws_permit_data <- read_csv(file.path(data_dir, "osds/shared-data/2009_Present_IWSList_Permits.csv"))


# filter out just the permits in Hawaii, and create permit ID tracker

iws_hi_permits <- iws_permit_data %>% 
  mutate(tmk_char = as.character(TMK)) %>% 
  filter(str_starts(tmk_char,"3")) %>% 
  rename(full_taxid = tmk_char) %>%  
  rowid_to_column("permit_id") # 7347

tmks_permits <- iws_hi_permits$full_taxid

# execute join to see which tmks have dwell data

iws_hi_dwell_join <- inner_join(iws_hi_permits, allyears_hi_dwell, by = "full_taxid") %>% 
  distinct() # 69630 rows, 6011 TMKS
# also filter, this should have fewer rows but the same number of tmks

iws_hi_dwell_join_norepeats <- iws_hi_permits %>% 
  filter(full_taxid %in% allyears_hi_dwell$full_taxid) #6242 rows, 6011 tmks YAY

# now identify permits that donʻt have dwell data, and save 

iws_hi_NOdwell <- iws_hi_permits %>% 
  filter(full_taxid %!in% iws_hi_dwell_join$full_taxid) # 1105

write_csv(iws_hi_NOdwell,
         file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/qaqc/hi_iwspermits_nodwellinginfo.csv"))

```

**Results so Far**:
- There were 7347 permits issued for HI island over the past 10 years
- 6242 have dwelling information, and this represents 6011 tmks
- 1105 do not have dwelling information

### Step 2b: Identifying Upgrade Scenarios

Here we will work to identify easy, tricky and hard scenarios. The steps
are as follows: 
1. Create a flag that flags if a TMK is repeated in the
same year or different year 
2. Count up scenarios and save

```{r}


# working with just the permit data, analyze duplicates for 1 permit issued to same place, and which years

iws_hi_permits$is_duplicate <- duplicated(iws_hi_permits$TMK) | duplicated(iws_hi_permits$TMK, fromLast = TRUE)
  
iws_hi_permits_dups <- filter(iws_hi_permits, is_duplicate == TRUE) # 791

iws_hi_permits_cl <- iws_hi_permits %>% 
  clean_names() %>%
  mutate(approval_date = mdy(final_approval_date),
         year = year(approval_date))

# create flag indicating if the duplicate is for the same year, or a different year

iws_hi_permits_flag <- iws_hi_permits_cl %>% 
  group_by(full_taxid) %>% 
  mutate(
    n_rows = n(),
    n_year = n_distinct(year)
  ) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(
    osds_flag = case_when(
      n_rows > 1 & n_year > 1 ~ "possbile update or later addition",
      n_rows > 1 & n_year == 1 ~ "possible multiple osds permits",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

check_dups_again <- filter(iws_hi_permits_flag, is_duplicate == TRUE)

# count up the different scenarios

iws_hi_scenarios <- iws_hi_permits_flag %>% 
  group_by(osds_flag) %>% 
  summarize(
    total_tmks = length(unique(full_taxid))
  )

# not saving for now


```

**RESULTS**
- 791 of the permits issued since 2010 are for duplicate TMKS, representing 262 tmks
- 131 are for possible upgrades or additions
- 131 are for possible multiple osds per tmk per year

- 6556 are for single permits corresponding to single tmks

### Step 3: Assign Class to Permits

The assignment of class is based on a previously determined scheme by
Whittier and El Kadi (2014). The scheme is as follows:

Class I = Any system receiving soil treatment, with disposal types as
bed, trench, and infiltration chambers 
Class II = Septic system discharging into seepage pit. This effluent only gets primary treatment. 
Class III = Aerobic units discharging into a seepage pit. The effluent received primary and secondary treatment. 
Class IV = Cesspools, no treatment

For HI, we have the following unique scenarios:
- Cesspool - existing
- "Other" with bed disposal?



```{r}

library(janitor)

# disposal types by treatment

minimal_treatment <- c("Seepage Pit",
                       "Cesspool-New")

primary_treatment <- c("Bed",
                       "Trench",
                       "Infiltrators / Chambers",
                       "ET Bed-Irrigation System",
                       "Presby")

unknown_treatment <- c("Other","Unknown")

combo_treatment <- c("Combination of two types")


# apply to hi data. For H

iws_hi_permits_withclass <- iws_hi_permits_flag %>%
  clean_names() %>% 
  #filter(is.na(osds_flag)) %>% 
  mutate(osds_class = case_when(
    permit_type == "Septic Tank" & disposal_type %in% primary_treatment ~"1",
    permit_type == "Septic Tank" & disposal_type %in% minimal_treatment ~"2",
    permit_type == "Septic Tank" & disposal_type %in% unknown_treatment ~ "2", 
    permit_type == "Septic Tank" & disposal_type %in% combo_treatment ~ "1", 
    permit_type %in% c("Compost Toilet","Gray Water System","Compost Toilet/Gray Water System") & disposal_type %in% c("Other","Unknown")  ~ "3",
    permit_type %in% c("Compost Toilet","Compost Toilet/Gray Water System") & disposal_type == "Bed" ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Gray Water System" & disposal_type %in% c("Bed","Trench") ~ "3",
    permit_type == "Aerobic Unit" & disposal_type %in% minimal_treatment ~ "4",
    permit_type == "Cesspool-New" ~ "4",
    permit_type == "Cesspool-Existing" ~ "4",
    permit_type == "Aerobic Unit" & disposal_type %in% primary_treatment ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Aerobic Unit" & disposal_type %in% unknown_treatment ~ "3",
    permit_type == "Aerobic Unit" & disposal_type %in% combo_treatment ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Presby (passive, NSF 40)" ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Holding Tank (Government Only)" ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Incinerating Toilet" ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Other" & disposal_type %in% primary_treatment ~ "1", #because it getting soil treatment?
    TRUE ~ "Can't assign MB" # the only one I couldnt assign just had some extra notes on the permit type
  )) %>% 
  mutate(osds_class = ifelse(osds_class == "Canʻt assign MB","1",osds_class)) # fix this one by hand




# need to think about this some more. Make sure I remember where I got the treatment groups.



```

### Step 4: Count addresses and permits by TMK & find min and max years

Parallel to the class assignment, here I examine the address column to
try and figure out if we can ID multiple building scenarios just from
the permit data.


```{r}

# how many addresses per TMK can we identify?
address_per_tmk <- iws_hi_permits_cl %>%
  group_by(full_taxid) %>% 
  mutate(address_full = ifelse(is.na(project_street_address2),
                               project_street_address,
                               paste(project_street_address,"-",project_street_address2))) %>% 
  mutate(address_lower = str_trim(str_to_lower(address_full))) %>% # in case theyʻve been entereed differently 
  summarize(
    n_addresses = length(unique(address_lower)), # how many buildings on this TMK
    n_permits = length(permit_id), # how many permits have they applied for in this time period
    min_year = min(year),
    last_year = max(year) # when these permits were issued
  ) # write this one out

# how many TMKS have more than one building?
nrow(address_per_tmk[address_per_tmk$n_addresses > 1, ]) #153

# does it matter if this is in lower case?

nrow(address_per_tmk[address_per_tmk$n_addresses > 1, ]) # 147


# add flag, at the TMK level 
address_per_tmk_flag <- address_per_tmk %>% 
  mutate(building_permit_scenario = case_when(
    n_addresses == 1 & n_permits == 1  ~ "One building, one permit",
    n_addresses == 1 & n_permits > 1 ~ "One buidling, multiple permits",
    n_addresses > 1 & n_permits == 1 ~ "Multiple buildings, one permit",
    n_addresses > 1 & n_permits > 1 ~ "Multiple buildings, Mulitple permits"
  ),
  year_scenario = case_when(
    last_year == min_year ~ "All the same year",
    TRUE ~ "Mulitple Years"
  ))


scenario_summary <- address_per_tmk_flag %>% 
  group_by(building_permit_scenario,year_scenario) %>% 
  summarize(
    tmk_per_scenario = n()
  )

# write these out
write_csv(address_per_tmk,
         file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/qaqc/hi_permits_and_buildings_pertmk.csv"),
         append = FALSE)


write_csv(scenario_summary,
         file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/qaqc/hi_building_scenario.csv"),
         append = FALSE)

# dont' forget to write the data

easys <- address_per_tmk_flag %>% 
  filter(building_permit_scenario == "One building, one permit") #6556

iws_hi_permits_easyscenario <- iws_hi_permits_withclass %>% 
  filter(tmk %in% easys$full_taxid) %>% 
  mutate(dwell_flag = ifelse(full_taxid %in% iws_hi_dwell_join$full_taxid,"Dwelling","Other")) %>% 
  select(-n_rows,-n_year, -osds_flag) #6556

write_csv(iws_hi_permits_easyscenario,
         file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/iws_hi_permits_easyscenario.csv"),
         append = FALSE)

```

**Results!**
- 6556 are one building, one permit. Yay! this matches what we got above
- 147 of the permits are for tmks with multiple buildings
- 38 of those tmks applied for their permits all in the same year
- 109 of those tmks applied for permits over more than one year
- 115 are for one building, but either multiple permits in the same year (N = 93) or over multiple years (N = 22)


## Compare to Past Datasets to Complete the Time Series

We have to bring in the past OSDS dataset to have a record of what each
tmk was bedroom wise and class wise prior to 2009 (which is when our
permit data starts). Without it, we can only track changes and upgrades
within the 2009 - 2020. Weʻll add this as a column. Once we do this, we
can generate cesspool upgrade list.

There are two main categories of comparison from Step 2; 
- Easy situations where we have one building, one permit per tmk 
- More complex ones.

### A) EASY scenario compare to OTP (2010 timestamp)

Let's start with the **easy list**. We'll read in the old OSDS dataset and
assume that what ever is recorded for that tmk in there is what it was
before 2010. If our new dataset has something different, we know its
changed. Important Assumption from Julia's work: if a location goes from
septic, or better, to CESSPOOL is probably wrong?

First read in most recently available data for Kauai and Explore:

```{r}

hi_otp <- read_csv(file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/large-input-data/OSDS_HIGIS_2010/On-site_Sewage_Disposal_Systems_-_Hawaii_Island.csv"))

unique(hi_otp$class)

```

So the Hawaii database has a similar format to the others, but also has a column with "source", indicating that someone has already gone through the processes of bringing in additional information for TMKS not in the Dwelling Assessment. This means that we should use this for our "mismatches" in the new data. There are also notes for all the commercial properties which is great!

UNFORTUNATELY there is no information about how effluent was calculated for non dwells as far as I can tell, but maybe some snooping around later will fix that. And, is a good reason to apply a standardized approach that matches the other islands.

We also have these! Which are helpful:

PITT Code Values:   0  Timeshare (Maui only)   100’s*  Improved Residential   200’s  Apartment   300’s  Commercial   400’s  Industrial   500’s  Agricultural and Rural   600’s   Conservation   700’s   Hotel and Resort   800’s**  Unimproved Residential   900’s  Homeowner    999   Multiple PITT Codes for a single TMK   1000’s  Commercialized Residential (Maui only)      *  Kauai:  100 = Improved and Unimproved Residential   **  Kauai:  800 = Homestead Properties 

Also: lots of -9999 in class? And no class 4 or 5. That makes no sense. 

Some of this data is messy and yuck but there is also a lot of helpful work that it looks like the department of health did in 2017 (or Joey did?) 

Another weird thing about this data is that they dropped the year column. 

We only have classes 1 - 4 in this data. From the metadata, this
represents:

-   CLASS_I: Class I OSDS are those systems where the effluent is
    subjected to soil treatment
-   CLASS_II: Class II OSDS are septic systems discharging to a seepage
    pit.\
-   CLASS_III: Class III OSDS are aerobic systems discharging to a
    seepage pit.
-   CLASS_IV: Class IV OSDS are cesspools.\
-   EFFLUENT: The total effluent flux in million gallons per day
    discharged within the TMK parcel.
    
    
The `osds_class` column also does not have any 4s, just 1-3, and -9999. I'll use the same additive coding here as I did with Maui Nui, Kauai (and eventually Oahu): 

| Combination                           | Sum |
|---------------------------------------|-----|
| Class 1                               | 1   |
| Class 2                               | 2   |
| Class 1 + Class 2                     | 3   |
| Class 3                               | 4   |
| Class 1 + Class 3                     | 5   |
| Class 2 + Class 3                     | 6   |
| Class 1 + Class 2 + Class 3           | 7   |
| Class 4                               | 8   |
| Class 1 + Class 4                     | 9   |
| Class 2 + Class 4                     | 10  |
| Class 1 + Class 2 + Class 4           | 11  |
| Class 3 + Class 4                     | 12  |
| Class 1 + Class 3 + Class 4           | 13  |
| Class 2 + Class 3 + Class 4           | 14  |
| Class 1 + Class 2 + Class 3 + Class 4 | 15  |

```{r}
library(janitor)

hi_otp_clean <- hi_otp %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  select(tmk, starts_with("class"), "osds_qty") # n = 13351 !

# read in the "easy scenario" new data, which are examples of one building and one permit TMKS. check for any duplciates

onebuilding_onepermit <- read.csv(file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/iws_hi_permits_easyscenario.csv"))

onebuilding_onepermit_distinct <- onebuilding_onepermit %>% 
  select(-permit_id) %>% 
  distinct() # none, cool!


# -----------  Q1:  do all these new ones exist in the old data? if not, then they are NEW osds builds ------------- #

otp_hi_filtered_byOBOP <- hi_otp_clean %>% 
  mutate(tmk = as.integer(tmk)) %>% 
  filter(tmk %in% onebuilding_onepermit$tmk) %>% 
  distinct() %>% # KEY: remove EXACT duplicates. We are treating these as errors
  rowid_to_column("newbuild_permit_id") %>% 
  mutate(year_issued = 2010) %>% # note this isn't right, just a place hodler for "pre 2010" to maintain consistent data structure in this column 
  mutate(change_flag = "new permit detected since otp") #2337


otp_kauai_NOTinOBOP <- hi_otp_clean %>%
  mutate(tmk = as.integer(tmk)) %>% 
  filter(tmk %!in% onebuilding_onepermit$tmk) %>% 
  rowid_to_column("old_permit_id") %>% 
  mutate(change_flag = "no new permit application since otp") 
  

write_csv(otp_kauai_NOTinOBOP,
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/otp_osds_wo_permitupgrade_hi.csv")) 


# -----------  Q2:  Which of the new builds are new OSDS, rather than builds on tmks with existing OSDS? ------------- #


onebuilding_onepermit_NEW_since2010 <- onebuilding_onepermit %>% 
  filter(tmk %!in% otp_hi_filtered_byOBOP$tmk) # 4219?? wow

length(unique(onebuilding_onepermit_NEW_since2010$tmk)) #4219 

# use set diff to see if its the same
tmks_not_inbob <- setdiff(onebuilding_onepermit$tmk, otp_hi_filtered_byOBOP$tmk) #4219 YAY

onebuilding_onepermit_NEW_since2010_otherway <- onebuilding_onepermit %>% 
  filter(tmk %in% tmks_not_inbob) 


write_csv(onebuilding_onepermit_NEW_since2010_otherway,
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/hi_osds_new_since_otp.csv"))

# --------------- Old Data: Data Reshape ------------------------------------- #


# Here I take the tmks present in OTP AND the new permit data, which represent upgrades. I reassign class to match the additive encoding schema, and then pivot wider. 



otp_hi_filtered_byOBOP_wide <- otp_hi_filtered_byOBOP %>% 
  select(-class) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("class"), names_to = "class", values_to = "quantity") %>% 
  filter(quantity != 0) %>% 
  rename(ttl_osds_2010 = osds_qty) %>% 
  mutate(osds_class_otp = case_when(
    class == "class_iv" ~ 8, # cesspool 
    class == "class_iii" ~ 4,
    class == "class_ii" ~ 2,
    class == "class_i" ~ 1
  )) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c("newbuild_permit_id","tmk","ttl_osds_2010"), 
              names_from = c("year_issued","class"), values_from = c("quantity"))



dups_check <- otp_hi_filtered_byOBOP_wide %>% mutate(duplicated = duplicated(tmk)) # none

otp_hi_morethan1osds <- otp_hi_filtered_byOBOP_wide %>% 
  filter(ttl_osds_2010 > 1) #311

# now, add the encoding 

otp_hi_filtered_byOBOP_wideENC <- otp_hi_filtered_byOBOP %>% 
  select(-class) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("class"), names_to = "class", values_to = "quantity") %>% 
  filter(quantity != 0) %>% 
  rename(ttl_osds_2010 = osds_qty) %>% 
  mutate(osds_class_otp = case_when(
    class == "class_iv" ~ 8, # cesspool 
    class == "class_iii" ~ 4,
    class == "class_ii" ~ 2,
    class == "class_i" ~ 1
  )) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c("newbuild_permit_id","tmk","ttl_osds_2010"), names_from = c("year_issued","class"), values_from = c("osds_class_otp")) %>%
  mutate(combo_code = rowSums(across(starts_with("2010")), na.rm = TRUE))

otp_hi_filtered_byOBOP_longENC <- otp_hi_filtered_byOBOP_wideENC %>% # collapse the wide columns
  select(-starts_with("2010"), -newbuild_permit_id)


# --------------- New Data: Data Reshape ------------------------------------- #


# now pivot the NEW data, for now just the "easy", that is also in OTP, one building one permit category, wider to match

onebuild_onepermit_inbob <- onebuilding_onepermit%>% 
  filter(tmk %in% otp_hi_filtered_byOBOP$tmk)

onebuild_onepermit_hi_wide <- onebuild_onepermit_inbob %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c("permit_id","tmk"), names_from = "year", values_from = c("permit_type","osds_class"))

dups_obop_hi <- onebuild_onepermit_hi_wide %>% mutate(duplicated = duplicated(tmk)) # no duplicates. great. 


# -------------- Combine:  Join our two wide tables together ----------------------------------- #

# IMPORTANT note: since 493 of the bob data have more than one OSDS, but the new data here are examples of just one building, one new permit, if any of the new data match to the old ones with more than one osds, weʻll have to make an assumption about which one was updated in this new data. 

all_osds_present_inboth <- left_join(dups_obop_hi, otp_hi_filtered_byOBOP_longENC, by = c("tmk"))

# so the next analysis will determine the most recent year a tmk was upgraded. We can add a flag for if there was an upgrade and there are multiple OSDS on the property. hoping that most of these did not have an upgrade. 


all_permit_present_inboth_long <- all_osds_present_inboth %>% 
  rename(otp_class_2010 = combo_code) %>% # this is what it was in 2010
  select(-starts_with("permit_type")) %>% # we dont need this right now
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("osds"),
               names_to = "year",
               values_to = "class",
               values_drop_na = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(
    year_num = as.integer(str_remove(year, "osds_class_"))  # extract numeric year rather than colname with year in it
  )


# here we'll use some logic to create a yes/no flag if upgraded, and a specific text flag for what kind of upgrade it was 


last_permit_persentinboth <- all_permit_present_inboth_long %>% 
  group_by(tmk) %>% 
  slice_max(year_num, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>% # get the latest year we have records for a given tmk
  mutate(class_last = as.numeric(class),
         class_last_year = year_num,
         class_otp = as.numeric(otp_class_2010)) %>% 
  mutate(upgrade_yn = case_when(
    class_last < class_otp & class_otp %in% c(1,2,4,8) ~ "upgrade occured on a single osds",
    class_last < class_otp & class_otp %!in% c(1,2,4,8) ~ "change occured on one of many existing osds",
    class_last == class_otp & class_otp %in% c(1,2,4,8) & class_last_year > 2010 ~ "addition",
    class_last == class_otp & class_otp %in% c(1,2,4,8) & class_last_year <= 2010 ~ "data overlap",
    class_last > class_otp  ~ "check class assignment"
  )) %>% 
  mutate(cesspool_upgrade = case_when(
    class_otp == 8 & class_last < 4 ~ "cesspool upgraded",
    class_otp %in% c(9,10,11,12,13,14,15) & class_last < 4 ~ "maybe cesspool upgraded - multiple existing osds",
    class_last == 4 & class_last_year > 2010 ~ "new cesspool permit",
    class_otp == 4 & class_last == 4 & class_last_year %in% c(2009,2010) ~ "duplicate, not upgraded",
    class_otp %!in% c(9,10,11,12,13,14,15) ~ "na"
  ))


# save! remember, we need to do this for the tricky and hard scenarios, and non dwells, as well
write_csv(last_permit_persentinboth,
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/hi_easy_possible_OSDSupgrades_withflag.csv"))

```

So there are a number here where there are more than one cesspool - we
may want to make an assumption that if there is one new permit for
something better than a cesspool (ie a septic tank), its replacing both
cesspools? OR, again another place for sensitivity analysis.

Also an important assumption: if there is a more recent application for
a place with cesspools, would that be for an ADDITIONAL cesspool or to
re-build one of them? not as important for effluent calculation, but
important for Chris and Aimee's work.

Last step! Tally up the changes and record as results below.

```{r}


upgrade_tally <- last_permit_persentinboth %>% 
  group_by(upgrade_yn) %>% 
  summarize(
    total_n = n()
  )

cesspool_upgrade_tally <-  last_permit_persentinboth %>% 
  group_by(cesspool_upgrade) %>% 
  summarize(
    total_n = n()
  )



```


WITHOUT COUNTING our more difficult scenarios: we have recorded 1514
upgrades   
351 possible additions or replacements of same kind   
114 where a change occurred on a tmk with many existing osds.

We also have 354 data overlaps, which I'll make sure aren't different,
and then delete duplicates.   
There are 4 where we record a "last class" that is a class lower than OTP. Need to double check these.

Of the upgrades (N = 1514), 
- 1195 are cesspool upgrades. 
- 101 are upgrades that occured on tks with many osds, of which one was a cesspool
- 133 are new cesspool permits since 2010


### B) NON DWELL scenarios

The old Hawaii osds data alread has categorized non dwells to some extent. Here I'll see how many of the new, non-dwell permits correspond to these old-places.

```{r}

# read in the non dwells - ie new permits for which we did not have any dwelling information

hi_permits_nodwellinfo <- read_csv(file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/qaqc/hi_iwspermits_nodwellinginfo.csv")) %>% clean_names() #1105


# hi otp commercial
hi_otp_commercial <- hi_otp %>% 
  filter(!is.na(commercial)) %>% 
  select(tmk, commercial, osds_qty, starts_with("class"), effluent,ttl_bdrms,source) %>%
  rename_with(~ paste0(.x, "_from_otp"), .cols = -1)
  

# left join, with hi
hi_newpermits_plusotpinfo <- left_join(hi_permits_nodwellinfo, hi_otp_commercial, by = "tmk")

# how many of the missing permits did we snag?

got_info <- hi_newpermits_plusotpinfo %>% filter(!is.na(commercial_from_otp)) # 289 only

# try another way- filter

hi_newpermits_noDwellfiltered <- hi_permits_nodwellinfo %>% 
  filter(tmk %in% hi_otp_commercial$tmk) # 289. same. 


# what about the rest of these? are the in the full otp, not filtered, dataset?

not_got_info <- hi_newpermits_plusotpinfo %>% filter(is.na(commercial_from_otp)) #816

hi_otp_filtered_byNGI <- hi_otp %>% 
  filter(tmk %in% not_got_info$tmk) %>%

# any others we did not account for? no

######### save the hi_otp by NGI so we can recombine with other dwelling data ################

write_csv(hi_otp_filtered_byNGI,
          file.path())

```

Ok! So, the Non-dwelling data is somewhat solved for Big Island. Here is the breakdown:
- 289 are known commercial locations
- 816 are not known commercial locations, but whoever updated this last has marked all of them with source = something other than Dwell Data. But the good news is that we now have all the info needed to calculate old effluent + if these were upgraded!

```{r}

# create the two tables for the commercial locations

########### table 1: tmk + key identifying info

table_1 <- got_info %>% 
  select(permit_id,tmk, island, starts_with("project"), final_approval_date, commercial_from_otp)

############# table 2: class by year. we need to assign class to the new data, and reshape the old data. 

# disposal types by treatment

minimal_treatment <- c("Seepage Pit",
                       "Cesspool-New")

primary_treatment <- c("Bed",
                       "Trench",
                       "Infiltrators / Chambers",
                       "ET Bed-Irrigation System",
                       "Presby")

unknown_treatment <- c("Other","Unknown")

combo_treatment <- c("Combination of two types")

hi_commercial_odsd_YearClasstable <- got_info %>% 
  select(permit_id, tmk, project_street_address, project_street_address2, final_approval_date, permit_type, disposal_type, ends_with("from_otp")) %>% 
  select(-class_from_otp) %>% 
  mutate(new_osds_class = case_when(
    permit_type == "Septic Tank" & disposal_type %in% primary_treatment ~"1",
    permit_type == "Septic Tank" & disposal_type %in% minimal_treatment ~"2",
    permit_type == "Septic Tank" & disposal_type %in% unknown_treatment ~ "2", 
    permit_type == "Septic Tank" & disposal_type %in% combo_treatment ~ "1", 
    permit_type %in% c("Compost Toilet","Gray Water System","Compost Toilet/Gray Water System") & disposal_type %in% c("Other","Unknown")  ~ "3",
    permit_type %in% c("Compost Toilet","Compost Toilet/Gray Water System") & disposal_type == "Bed" ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Gray Water System" & disposal_type %in% c("Bed","Trench") ~ "3",
    permit_type == "Aerobic Unit" & disposal_type %in% minimal_treatment ~ "4",
    permit_type == "Cesspool-New" ~ "4",
    permit_type == "Cesspool-Existing" ~ "4",
    permit_type == "Aerobic Unit" & disposal_type %in% primary_treatment ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Aerobic Unit" & disposal_type %in% unknown_treatment ~ "3",
    permit_type == "Aerobic Unit" & disposal_type %in% combo_treatment ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Presby (passive, NSF 40)" ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Holding Tank (Government Only)" ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Incinerating Toilet" ~ "1",
    permit_type == "Other" & disposal_type %in% primary_treatment ~ "1", #because it getting soil treatment?
    TRUE ~ "Can't assign MB" # the only one I couldnt assign just had some extra notes on the permit type
  )) %>% 
  mutate(approval_date = mdy(final_approval_date),
         year = year(approval_date))

hi_commercial_odsd_new_clean <- hi_commercial_odsd_YearClasstable %>% 
  select(permit_id, tmk,starts_with("project"),final_approval_date,year,new_osds_class) %>% 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c("permit_id","tmk","project_street_address","project_street_address2","final_approval_date"), names_from = year, values_from = new_osds_class)

hi_commercial_osds_olds <- got_info %>% 
  select(permit_id,tmk,project_street_address, project_street_address2,final_approval_date, ends_with("from_otp")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = starts_with("class"), names_to = "class", values_to = "quantity") %>% 
  filter(quantity != -9999) %>% 
  mutate(year = 2010) %>% 
  rename(ttl_osds_2010 = osds_qty_from_otp) %>% 
  mutate(osds_class_otp = case_when(
    str_detect(class, "class_iv") ~ 8, # cesspool 
    str_detect(class, "class_iii") ~ 4,
    str_detect(class, "class_ii") ~ 2,
    str_detect(class, "class_i") ~ 1
  )) %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c("permit_id","tmk","project_street_address","final_approval_date","ttl_osds_2010"), names_from = c("class","year"), values_from = c("osds_class_otp")) %>%
  select(-class_from_otp_2010) %>% 
  mutate(combo_code = rowSums(across(starts_with("class")), na.rm = TRUE))

# join together

hi_commercial_olds_cl <- hi_commercial_osds_olds %>% 
  select(-starts_with("class")) %>% 
  rename(prior_class = combo_code)


table_2_final <- left_join(hi_commercial_olds_cl,hi_commercial_odsd_new_clean, by = c(
  "permit_id",
  "tmk",
  "project_street_address",
  "final_approval_date"
))

# use anti join to check that all of info in table 1 are in table 2

missing_rows <- anti_join(table_1, table_2_final, by = c(
  "permit_id",
  "tmk",
  "project_street_address",
  "final_approval_date"
)) # 0, yay!!



# save to drop box

write_csv(table1,
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/commercial_finaltables/hi_comm_table1.csv"))

write_csv(table_2_final,
          file.path(driver_dir,"4_OSDS_N_Runoff/output-data/commercial_finaltables/hi_comm_table2.csv"))

```


### c) TRICKY and HARD scenarios

For the tricky and hard scenarios, we have to do a bit of extra data wrangling. 

```{r}





```
